title: Stage Latency Trellis — sampling & annotated lab notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures an ad-hoc investigation using an incremental span-sampler ("trellis" sampling) to profile end-to-end request latency across the serving runtime. The goal: get a compact but representative set of traces that expose common stage-level hotspots at p50/p95/p99 and to propose short experiments that can reduce tail latency without regressing cost.

High-level summary (observations):
- p50: 42ms, p95: 180ms, p99: 520ms for text-gen route /v1/generate (default model v1.4-qa).
- Breakdown skew: tokenize + input-encode consistently ~3-8ms; model-forward (kernel execution + memcpy) dominates median but not always the tail. At p99, the dominant contributors are: batch-wait (queueing) + KV cache miss handling + final egress serialization.
- Notable: A fraction (~6%) of p99 traces show a KV-cache vacuum event where a concurrent eviction and refill causes a synchronous disk read path (~120–240ms) — this correlates to hosts running at >85% memory utilization.
- Another class (~2%) are micro-coldstart traces where worker process spin-up and JIT warmups add 200–400ms.

Sampling methodology (trellis/span-sampler):
- We ran a randomized stratified sample across: sequence length buckets (<=64, 65-256, 257-1024), model_variant (v1.4-qa, v1.4-opt-4bit), and route QPS buckets (low <50, medium 50-250, high >250).
- Sampler config: keep 1/200 at p50 region, 1/50 at p95 region, and 1/10 for p99 candidates; additionally bias-sample traces with >200ms total latency at 10x rate.
- Total traces collected: 12,400 over 48h (Feb 8–9, 2025).

Representative per-stage annotated numbers (median / p95 / p99; numbers in ms):
- Tokenize: 2 / 5 / 12
- Input encode (protobuf + routing): 5 / 18 / 35
- Queue wait (batching): 8 / 60 / 220
- KV cache lookup (in-memory hit): 1 / 3 / 10
- KV cache miss (disk path): 40 / 110 / 210
- Model forward (kernel + memcpy): 18 / 70 / 130
- Post-process + filter: 3 / 10 / 28
- Egress serialization: 3 / 12 / 80
Notes: p99 inflation mainly from queue wait and occasional KV miss + egress serialization anomalies.

Trace archetypes discovered (examples):
- A: "smooth median" (68% of traces) — queue wait <15ms, KV hit, model forward 10–25ms.
- B: "batched tail" (18%) — high queue wait (60–220ms) during transient QPS bursts; model-forward relatively stable.
- C: "kv-miss slab" (6%) — immediate KV miss causes a synchronous refill path (40–240ms) and sometimes blocks other traces in same worker.
- D: "worker spin/coldstart" (2%) — worker spin-up + JIT cost; correlated with node recycling and a single-process restart script.
- E: "egress stall" (6%) — serialization stalls caused by large structured outputs or inefficient JSON emitter fallback.

Trace snippet (example, flattened timeline):
trace_id: t-0a4f2 | seq_len: 512 | model: v1.4-qa
- tokenize: 3ms
- input-encode: 9ms
- queue-wait: 190ms
- kv-lookup: hit (2ms)
- model-forward: 96ms
- post-process: 8ms
- egress: 12ms
total: 320ms

Correlation notes and signals used:
- Memory utilization per-worker (host metrics) correlated with KV miss slab events (Pearson r ~0.62).
- Pod restart logs show that ~70% of coldstart class traces come from nodes with recent oomkill/recycler events in last 5m.
- Burst windows correspond to autoscaler throttle oscillations in two AZs (networked load spikes followed by short period of backpressure).

Quick investigative commands (internal ops):
- Fetch trellis sample: tracetool query --sample trellis-20250208 --filter route=/v1/generate --out traces.json
- Inspect trace breakdown: tracetool summarize --input traces.json --group-by stage --quantiles 50,95,99
- KV miss walk: kvcache-inspect --host node-17 --time 2025-02-08T14:32:00Z --tail 1000
- Node busy snapshot: iget-metrics --node node-17 --span 5m --metrics cpu,memory,qdepth

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Queue wait tail is primarily due to batching policy that allows long waits to accumulate during burst smoothing; lowering max_wait_ms for high-priority routes should reduce p99 at cost of throughput.
2) KV miss slab events are exacerbated by memory pressure on nodes; increasing in-memory slab or moving small-model KV to SSD-backed LRU async refill will lower tail.
3) Egress stalls come from large JSON escapes when outputs include base64 attachments; streaming-emit optimization could reduce egress p99.
4) Coldstart traces tied to recycler timing — add staggered restart window to avoid correlated restarts.

Small experiments to run (fast, 1–2 day turnaround):
- Experiment A (canary): reduce max_wait_ms from 100ms -> 40ms for route /v1/generate for 10% traffic; monitor p50/p95/p99 and throughput. Owner: Ethan. (JIRA-9221)
- Experiment B (infra tweak): bump per-worker heap target for KV from 12GB -> 14GB on candidate pool; shadow-run for 24h. Owner: Marco.
- Experiment C (egress): enable streaming JSON emitter on beta variant; measure p99 egress tail. Owner: Anika.

Runbook snippets for triage (if p99 increases suddenly):
1) Pull trellis sample window (last 30m) and compare stage quantiles.
2) If queue-wait increased >> check autoscaler and routing logs; if seen, scale up burst pool or reduce max_wait_ms.
3) If KV miss spike >> inspect host memory and eviction metrics; if concurrent, schedule bump.
4) If worker coldstarts spike >> correlate with pod restarts and check recycler job.

Outstanding questions / unknowns:
- What is the exact cache refill latency distribution on SSD-backed refill paths? Need traces that instrument async refill latency end-to-end.
- Is there a safe policy to preferentially route long sequences to larger workers to avoid queue buildup? (scheduling policy change)
- Clarify whether egress emitter fallback is triggered by specific content shapes — need content-sandboxed traces.

Notes to self / informal:
- Sampling bias: the trellis sampler still slightly oversamples high-seq traces (we intend to correct for this in weightings).
- Remember to attach dashboard snapshots to JIRA ticket for Experiment A.
- Possible low-effort quick win: add simple heuristic to bypass batch queue if predicted token cost > threshold.

Appendix (links & artifacts):
- Shadow-run traces (S3): s3://redwood-traces/trellis/2025-02-08/
- Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/serving/latency/trellis-20250208
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1428

Next steps (owner/action/due):
- Run Experiment A canary and collect 48h results. Owner: Ethan Zhao / due 2025-03-07.
- Prepare async KV refill microbenchmark and capture refill latencies. Owner: Marco Ruiz / due 2025-03-10.
- Prototype streaming egress emitter on beta model. Owner: Anika Patel / due 2025-03-09.

If anything urgent pops during the canary, ping #eng-serving-runtime and add an ops flag to revert max_wait_ms via feature flag.

End of notes.
